The /proc/<pid>/status file doesn't exist for the child PID?! That's strange — unless the process is a zombie or the /proc entry requires... hmm. Oh! Maybe the sandbox/container has a restricted /proc. Whatever — the process DID run and complete correctly (11 output lines, exit 0).

Let me measure the thread count differently: run the analyzer in-process and check the thread count of the current process via `len(os.listdir('/proc/self/task'))`.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/dev && python3 -c "
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')
print('threads at start:', len(os.listdir('/proc/self/task')))
import analyze, genbig
x = genbig.gen(0, 'wide')
analyze.process_line(json.dumps(x, separators=(',', ':')).encode())
print('threads after one big instance:', len(os.listdir('/proc/self/task')))
x = genbig.gen(1, 'tight')
analyze.process_line(json.dumps(x, separators=(',', ':')).encode())
print('threads after two instances:', len(os.listdir('/proc/self/task')))
print('fds:', len(os.listdir('/proc/self/fd')))
"
